title: Avoid cloning and serializing unchanged retained messages on each persistence tick
outcome: After a durable baseline, session persistence captures, serializes and submits only changed message bodies while preserving transcript semantics, atomic durability and StateInner responsiveness; serialized payload metrics remain distinct from actual SQL row changes and physical device writes.
acceptance: After an initial durable baseline, production persistence of a session metadata-only change serializes and submits zero unchanged message rows/JSON bytes; append or edit of k messages serializes and submits only those changed/new messages, independent of unchanged retained transcript size, with explicit safe full-replacement handling for reorder/truncation/import and no on-disk schema change.

Deterministic isolated SQLite regressions measure serialized/submitted message rows and bytes separately from actual inserted/updated/deleted message rows, cover unchanged ticks, metadata-only changes, streaming edits, append, truncation/reorder and cold-prefix retention, and prove no lost, duplicated or reordered messages after reload.

Failure-before-commit, retry/reopen and concurrent message mutation preserve the existing transaction, watermark and fence semantics: no acknowledgement of uncommitted content, no skipped newer change, and exact message/order recovery after reload.

Production snapshot collection does not deep-clone or JSON-serialize unchanged retained message bodies while holding StateInner; deterministic phase-controlled regression verifies the lock boundary, and source/diagnostic analysis distinguishes collect-wait, collect-hold, serialize and SQL time without claiming w-d428 API-stall closure from payload counters alone.
Focused regressions and the full gate pass on the exact final input that lands, with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
